title: Variables for replacing a cloud LLM API with a self-hosted model on sensitive data

items.text: The actual threat model: which specific risk does self-hosting remove (retention, training on data, subprocessors, breach) and can it be handled contractually (e.g., zero retention) instead
paraphrases: Threat model: what exactly is the risk with the API today - retention, training on our data, subprocessors?
Can zero-data-retention terms address the CISO's concern without moving infrastructure?
Identify the specific risk self-hosting would remove.

items.text: Regulatory and contractual requirements: customer agreements, audits, data-protection obligations already satisfied by the vendor agreement
paraphrases: Contractual requirements from insurer customers and the data-protection agreement already in place.
Regulatory and audit obligations for medical records.
Compliance: what do customer contracts actually require?

items.text: Output quality on Northfold's own tasks: summaries and decision letters must be evaluated against the current API on a representative test set
paraphrases: Output quality: build an eval set of real summaries and letters and compare the open model with the API.
Accuracy and hallucination rate on medical-record summarization.
Capability gap between open-weight models and the current API on our tasks.

items.text: Self-hosting moves security responsibility in-house: access control, patching, logging, insider risk; it is not automatically more secure
paraphrases: Self-hosting isn't automatically safer: we take on patching, access control and insider risk.
Our own security posture for a GPU cluster vs the vendor's mature controls.
Attack surface moves in-house.

items.text: Total cost of ownership: GPUs, power, data-center space, staff and on-call vs per-token API cost at 40k docs/month
paraphrases: Total cost of ownership: GPUs, power, staff and on-call vs the current API bill.
Break-even point at 40,000 documents a month.
Capex for hardware vs per-token opex.

items.text: Operational capacity and skills: two engineers can't run a production GPU inference stack with 24/7 on-call, upgrades and monitoring
paraphrases: Two engineers can't also run a GPU inference platform with on-call.
MLOps skills and headcount needed to operate the stack.
Operational burden: upgrades, monitoring, incidents.

items.text: Capacity and latency at quarter-end peaks: sizing hardware for peak vs idle the rest of the time
paraphrases: Quarter-end peaks: owned hardware must be sized for peak volume and sits idle otherwise.
Throughput and latency under peak load.
Scalability vs the elastic cloud API.

items.text: Model licence terms of the open-weight model (commercial-use restrictions, acceptable-use clauses)
paraphrases: Open-weight model licence terms and commercial-use restrictions.
Acceptable-use clauses in the model licence.
Licensing: can we legally use the model for claims decisions?

items.text: Model lifecycle: keeping up with better models, re-validation on every upgrade, lock-in to an aging model
paraphrases: Model lifecycle: we'd have to upgrade and re-validate ourselves or fall behind the frontier.
Update cadence and re-validation burden for each new model version.
Risk of being stuck on an aging model.

items.text: Hybrid options: redaction/de-identification before the API, routing only the most sensitive documents to a local model
paraphrases: Hybrid: de-identify or redact records before sending them to the API.
Route only the most sensitive documents to a local model.
Tiered approach instead of all-or-nothing.

items.text: Decision-letter risk: errors in claim decisions affect people; human review, audit trails and explainability are needed whichever model is used
paraphrases: Claim decision letters affect claimants - human review and audit trails are needed regardless of hosting.
Liability for wrong decisions drafted by the model.
Explainability and appeals when letters contain errors.

items.text: Migration effort and risk: re-engineering prompts and pipelines, regression testing, parallel run and rollback
paraphrases: Migration effort: prompts and pipelines must be reworked and regression-tested.
Run both in parallel with a rollback plan before cut-over.
Transition risk and switching cost.

items.text: Vendor dependency/availability: outages, price changes or policy changes at the API vendor
paraphrases: Vendor dependency: API outages or price increases.
Availability and uptime of the API vs in-house.
Concentration risk on one vendor.
